newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Albright says U.S. to closely monitor HK elections.
newsitem.headline: Albright says U.S. to closely monitor HK elections.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said Washington would closely monitor China's promise to hold elections within a year for a new legislature for Hong Kong, which reverts to Beijing rule on Monday.

"We will watch closely to see if free and fair elections for a new legislature are conducted as promised at an early date," she said at a reception on Sunday held by U.S. Consul General to Hong Kong, Richard Boucher.
Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said that Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa told him on Sunday that his administration would hold elections next May.

It was the first time a specific month had been mentioned for polls to return the first elected legislature to replace the Beijing-appointed provisional chamber to be sworn in shortly after the handover of the British colony at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
Albright, among many dignitaries in the territory for the handover, reiterated her plans not to attend the swearing in of the new legislature.
"This sends a clear political message that the United States is and will remain a friend to democracy in Hong Kong and elsewhere," she said.
Boucher will represent the United States at the swearing in.

The provisional legislature will replace a body elected in 1995 under democratic reforms introduced by Hong Kong's last British governor Chris Patten. Albright said the United States would continue to care about the future of Hong Kong and urged that the rule of law, which has allowed the territory to prosper, be maintained.

"The message I bring on behalf of President (Bill) Clinton is that America cares about Hong Kong and will continue to care long after this week's fireworks are finished, the cameras are turned off and the partying is done," she said.
"The rule of law is what has allowed Hong Kong to scrape the sky. It is upon the continuation of the rule of law that its future aspirations depend."
